item.title: Jr Counsel Intern
item.description:
Role : : Jr Counsel(Legal) Intern
Location : On-site, Singapore

About HugoHub

Hello and Welcome!

HugoHub is the intelligent foundation for the future of finance, providing a modular banking platform that empowers financial institutions to move at speed.

Designed to simplify the path to digitisation for small and medium-sized banks, the platform consists of both backend core platform and frontend experience layer that offer a full suite of modular banking services through a single integration. By embedding intelligence and compliance directly into its architecture, HugoHub enables financial institutions to launch specialised products, automate back-office complexity, and scale with unparalleled efficiency.

HugoHub is a B2B platform with multiple offices across Singapore, India, United Kingdom, Indonesia, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It is owned by Atlas Consolidated Pte Ltd.

Atlas

Atlas Consolidated Pte Ltd. is Headquartered in Singapore.

A regulated entity with strong credentials

Atlas Consolidated Pte Ltd satisfies stringent corporate governance, operations, and regulatory integrity requirements to maintain licences from regulatory bodies, such as:

  • Monetary Authority of Singapore - Major Payment Institution licence and Financial Advisors licence

  • Ministry of Law, Singapore - Regulated Precious Metals Dealers licence

  • Visa Inc. - Principal Members Issuing licence

Who are we looking for ?

We are seeking an ambitious, detail-oriented Jr Counsel (Legal) Intern to support our legal and compliance functions in Singapore. You will gain hands-on experience working on commercial agreements, corporate governance, and regulatory matters within a fast-growing, multi-jurisdictional fintech environment.

How will you contribute to HugoHub?

  • Assist in drafting, reviewing, and negotiating a variety of commercial agreements, including non-disclosure agreements, service level agreements, and consultancy contracts.

  • Conduct supplier contract verification and vendor due diligence to ensure compliance with internal risk parameters and regulatory requirements.

  • Support general corporate legal matters, regulatory filings, and corporate governance obligations across HugoHub and Atlas Consolidated entities.

  • Research relevant financial regulations, licensing frameworks, data protection, and cross-border compliance matters affecting fintech operations.


Must have skills:

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) or equivalent legal qualification from a recognised university.

  • Strong foundational knowledge of contract law, legal drafting, and commercial terms.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with meticulous attention to detail.

  • Ability to manage confidential information with high integrity and discretion.

Good to have skills :

  • Familiarity with financial services regulations, payment licences, or fintech business models in Singapore and South East Asia.

  • Previous legal internship experience in a corporate legal department or law firm.

  • Understanding of data privacy and intellectual property principles.


HugoHub values being Responsible, Open, and Collaborative.

You should be passionate about what HugoHub stands for:

  • Honest, truthful and open communication at all times with the team members.

  • We are responsible to our customers, community, and team to help shape a more open, collaborative approach to wealth. This is how HugoHub hopes to make a difference and help us build better communities.

  • Shared responsibility is not only part of our approach to wealth but also a key part of working together. This shared responsibility allows for openness and candour between us as a team and in our customer relationship.

  • Good ideas can come from anywhere, so an open and collaborative dialogue between the HugoHub community (customers, team, and stakeholders alike) helps us all get the best from each other and makes a difference. Everyone is welcome to apply.


Curious To Know More

Find and follow us here: Linkedin

Join us on a mission to simplify complexity in finance through the use of applied, intelligent, deep technology!

item.title: Technical Program Manager
item.description:
The Technical Program Manager (TPM) is HugoHub's internal-facing role. They own delivery of complex, cross-functional technical programmes — ensuring the right things are built correctly, on time, and at scale across Engineering, Product, Design, QA, Compliance, and Operations.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for a TPM who combines deep technical fluency with programme management rigour and the ability to drive alignment across complex, multi-team organisations. The following qualities define someone who will thrive in this role:

  • Problem-Solving: Diagnoses root causes quickly, structures options clearly, and drives to a decision — even under ambiguity and time pressure.

  • Attention to Detail: Maintains rigour across programme plans, status reports, and technical decisions — because details missed at planning become issues in delivery.

  • Programme Ownership: Takes full accountability for programme outcomes. Drives forward proactively without waiting to be asked — and escalates early with context and options, not just problems.

  • Time Management: Manages multiple concurrent programmes across teams with different priorities, holding each to its commitments while keeping the broader delivery picture in focus.

  • Communication Skills: Translates fluently between engineering reality and business expectation — giving leadership what they need to decide, and giving engineering teams what they need to execute.

  • Adaptability: Restructures approach when priorities shift or scope changes — without losing programme momentum or stakeholder confidence.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Aligns Engineering, Product, Design, QA, Compliance, and Operations around shared programme goals — driving decisions and clearing blockers across team boundaries without direct authority.

  • Technical Translation: Converts engineering constraints, architectural decisions, and technical risks into clear business implications — enabling leadership to make informed, timely decisions.

  • Risk and Dependency Management:Identifies risks and dependencies before they become blockers. Builds mitigation plans proactively and communicates trade-offs clearly to the right stakeholders at the right time.

  • Technical Acumen: Understands system architecture, APIs, data pipelines, and the SDLC well enough to spot technical risks, challenge estimates credibly, and earn the trust of engineering teams.


What a “Technical Programme Manager” means to us

The Engine of Cross-Functional Delivery

The TPM is HugoHub's internal delivery engine. They translate strategic objectives into structured, executable programme plans — and then drive those plans to completion across Engineering, Product, Design, QA, Compliance, and Operations. A TPM at HugoHub is not a coordinator. They are a programme owner who holds teams accountable, surfaces risk early, and ensures nothing falls through the gaps between teams.


Core Responsibilities include

The core responsibilities of the TPM role at HugoHub:

  • Program Planning and Execution: Own end-to-end programme planning and execution — from scoping and goal definition through delivery and stabilisation. Define programme goals, success metrics, milestones, and resource requirements in collaboration with Engineering, Product, and leadership. Track progress in Jira using Agile and Scrum methodologies, maintaining a live view of programme health at all times.

  • Project Coordination: Serve as the central coordination point across all programme workstreams — ensuring Engineering, Product, Design, QA, Compliance, and Operations are aligned on scope, timelines, and priorities at every stage. Manage risks, dependencies, and blockers proactively; escalate to the right people with context and a clear recommendation.

  • Cross-functional collaboration: Drive alignment across Engineering, Product, Design, QA, Operations, and Compliance — from requirements definition through delivery. Identify blockers, assign ownership, and clear them. Influence and drive decision-making with senior leadership without direct authority over any of the contributing teams.

  • Stakeholder Communication: Own stakeholder communication across all levels — from Engineering sprint updates to leadership steering decks. Produce structured programme status reports (RAG health, milestones, risks, decisions needed). Act as the bridge between business objectives and engineering execution, translating in both directions with precision.

  • Technical Oversight: Maintain sufficient technical depth to evaluate architecture decisions, challenge estimates, identify technical risks before they surface in delivery, and engage credibly with engineering teams on design trade-offs and SDLC constraints.

  • Risk Management: Maintain a live risk and dependency register across all programmes. Identify risks early, assess business impact, develop mitigation plans, and communicate trade-offs to leadership with enough lead time to act — not after the fact.

  • Resource Management: Ensure the right engineering and cross-functional capacity is allocated to each programme. Identify resource constraints early and work with team leads and leadership to resolve them before they affect delivery timelines.

  • Quality Assurance: Hold programme deliverables to defined acceptance criteria and quality standards. Coordinate with QA on test planning, exit criteria, and defect prioritisation — ensuring quality is built into the programme, not bolted on at the end.

  • Continuous Improvement: Continuously identify and implement improvements to programme management practices, tooling, and ways of working across the TPM function and the broader delivery organisation. Share learnings across programmes.

  • Documentation and Reporting: Maintain accurate programme documentation — plans, status reports, risk registers, decision logs, and meeting records. Prepare and present programme updates to senior leadership, translating programme complexity into clear business narrative.

  • Mentorship: Coach and develop junior TPMs through structured feedback, shared programme experiences, and deliberate knowledge transfer. Raise the capability of the TPM function as a whole — not just your own programmes.


What we consider relevant qualifications, experience and knowledge

The experience and capabilities we look for:

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on technical programme management experience, owning complex cross-functional programmes end-to-end

  • Background in software engineering or a deeply technical role is strongly preferred — this experience underpins the technical credibility the role requires

  • Proven track record of driving cross-functional programmes to delivery — with measurable outcomes and demonstrable stakeholder management at senior level

  • Proficient in English both written and spoken

  • Experience in fintech, banking, or regulated technology environments is a strong plus

  • Proficiency in Agile and Scrum methodologies; experience running or coordinating sprints across multiple engineering teams

  • Proficiency in Jira for programme tracking, dependency management, and reporting

  • PMP, SAFe, or PRINCE2 certification is a plus; what matters more is demonstrated delivery at scale


Performance indicators to get you off to a great start

Quick Win — First 30 Days:

  • Map HugoHub's internal team structure, understand each function's role and how they interact in programme delivery

  • Learn HugoHub's programme management processes, tooling, and governance frameworks

  • Understand HugoHub's product portfolio, active programmes, and client landscape — building context fast enough to contribute to live programmes

  • Get hands-on with the systems and platforms used across teams — Jira, internal dashboards, communication and documentation tools


Finding Your Stride — 60 Days:

  • Independently manage at least one active programme — running cadence, tracking status, managing risks, and producing stakeholder updates without supervision

  • Build effective working relationships across Engineering, Product, Design, QA, and Compliance — with teams trusting you to coordinate their work fairly and accurately


Full Stride — 120 Days:

  • Own and drive multiple complex programmes simultaneously — building programme plans, managing cross-functional dependencies, and delivering to committed timelines with minimal escalation

  • Proactively identify risks and blockers across your programmes before they surface, assign ownership, and resolve them — with escalation as the exception, not the default

  • Identify and implement at least one meaningful improvement to HugoHub's programme management practices — contributing to the TPM function's ongoing development, not just your own programme execution

item.title: Implementation Specialist
item.description:
Implementation Specialist


Client Delivery & Programme Management Champion

The Implementation Specialist is HugoHub’s primary client-facing programme owner — the single point of accountability for taking a client from signed contract through to a fully stabilised, live deployment. This is a client relationship and programme management role as much as it is a technical one.


Core Focus: Own the client relationship end-to-end — from inception through delivery and handover. Drive alignment across Solution Engineering, Engineering, Design, TPM, Product, Compliance, QA, and Customer Success to ensure every commitment is delivered on time, in scope, and to the quality the client expects.


Detailed Responsibilities

Client Discovery & Scoping

  • Lead structured kickoff sessions with new clients to establish shared understanding of their business objectives, workflows, technical environment, integration dependencies, and success criteria.

  • Facilitate requirement-gathering workshops bringing client stakeholders and internal HugoHub teams (Solution Engineering, Product, Design) into a single aligned conversation — translating client needs into actionable technical requirements.

  • Drive all scoping discussions with precision — defining what is in scope, what is explicitly out of scope, and what carries risk of scope creep; document and get sign-off on all boundaries.

  • Author and finalise the Statement of Work (SOW) in collaboration with Solution Engineering and the commercial team, defining phases, workstreams, milestones, and acceptance criteria. Flag compliance or regulatory requirements early, looping in the Compliance team before solutioning begins.

Project Planning

  • Build detailed, milestone-driven programme plans covering all tasks, owners, dependencies, and timelines from discovery through go-live. Own the programme calendar: chair client cadence calls, internal sprint reviews with Engineering and QA, and cross-functional syncs with TPM and Product.

  • Maintain real-time project tracking in Jira, ensuring tasks are clearly assigned, statuses are current, and blockers are visible to all teams. Proactively surface risks and dependencies before they become problems — escalating with context, options, and a recommended path forward.

  • Produce structured weekly programme status reports for client leadership and internal stakeholders covering: RAG health, milestone progress, risks, decisions needed, and upcoming actions. Manage scope change requests formally — assessing impact and getting sign-off before absorbing any change.

Configuration & Deployment

  • Coordinate end-to-end across Solution Engineering, Engineering, Design, TPM, Product, Compliance, QA, and Customer Success — ensuring all teams are aligned on scope, timelines, and client expectations at every phase.

  • Work with Solution Engineers to translate client requirements into technical solution designs, reviewing architectures for completeness and flagging gaps against client expectations before Engineering begins build.

  • Partner with the TPM on all platform-level features and custom development — tracking dependencies, managing sprint commitments, and ensuring Engineering delivery aligns with the client programme timeline. Collaborate with Product and Design on any configuration or UX decisions specific to the client.

  • Engage Compliance on data handling and regulatory requirements before UAT. Coordinate QA on test planning and defect triage. Brief Customer Success fully ahead of handover — ensuring no context is lost at the transition point.

Testing & Quality Assurance

  • Define the overall test strategy in collaboration with QA. Conduct or oversee rigorous internal testing of the client’s configured environment, ensuring all known issues are resolved and exit criteria are met before involving the client.

  • Plan, schedule, and lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) — creating structured test scripts, managing the defect log, coordinating resolution across Engineering and QA, and communicating defect status and timelines clearly to the client. Drive formal UAT sign-off before go-live.

Training & Handover

  • Develop customised training materials tailored to the client’s specific configuration and user personas. Host onboarding sessions for administrators, power users, and end users — adjusting depth and format to each audience.

  • Own the go-live plan end-to-end: define the go-live checklist, coordinate the deployment window with Engineering and TPM, establish a hypercare support window, and lead the go-live event — serving as the client’s primary contact throughout and managing any real-time issues to resolution.

  • Manage the post-launch hypercare period, tracking early issues and providing the client with regular updates until the platform is fully stabilised. Execute a structured handover to Customer Success with full documentation of the client’s configuration, open items, known issues, and relationship context.

Client Relationship Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Serve as the primary, trusted point of contact for the client from kickoff through handover — owning all communication, meeting agendas, and follow-up actions. Build trusted relationships with client programme managers, technical leads, and business stakeholders at all levels.

  • Set and manage client expectations proactively — communicating changes to timelines, scope, or deliverables clearly and early, with options rather than just problems. Translate between HugoHub’s internal technical language and client business language fluently in both directions.

  • Gather continuous structured feedback from the client and route it to Product, Design, and Customer Success as input into HugoHub’s product development process. Conduct a formal implementation retrospective post-go-live and share learnings with the wider delivery team.

Ideal Candidate Profile

A highly organised, client-ownership-minded professional having 3 to 5 years of experience who combines strong programme management discipline with genuine technical credibility. The ideal candidate is as comfortable in a client steering committee as they are in an Engineering sprint review — and holds themselves accountable for the outcome of every engagement they own. We believe the following qualities are important for someone to thrive in this position:


  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Ability to think critically and make informed decisions.

  • Attention to Detail: Strong attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality results.

  • Client Ownership: Takes full accountability for the client relationship and programme outcome from day one through to handover. The client’s confidence in HugoHub during implementation is a direct reflection of how this person shows up.

  • Time Management: Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritise tasks effectively and meet deadlines.

  • Communication Skills: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders and convey complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Adaptability: Adaptive and accustomed to a fast-paced and dynamic working environment

  • Cross-Functional Influence: Aligns and drives urgency across Engineering, QA, Design, TPM, Product, Compliance, and Customer Success without direct authority. Owns the outcome while bringing structure and accountability to every team involved.

  • Technical Translation: The skill to abstract deep technical constraints into strategic business implications for non-technical audiences.

  • Proactive Risk Management: Identifies risks and blockers early, assesses their impact, and brings forward options — not just problems. Escalates to the right people with context and a recommended path forward.

  • Technical Acumen: Deep understanding of SDLC/SDLC, system architecture, Design and technologies; enables informed decisions and effective engineer engagement.

item.title: Product Security Engineer
item.description:
About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Product Security Engineer to join our team and help build security into every aspect of our product development lifecycle. In this role, you'll work closely with engineering, product, and DevOps teams to identify, assess, and mitigate security risks while enabling rapid and secure product delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Threat Modeling & Risk Assessment

  • Design and conduct comprehensive threat modeling sessions for new features and system architectures

  • Identify potential attack vectors and security vulnerabilities early in the development process

  • Collaborate with product and engineering teams to prioritize security requirements based on risk assessment

  • Develop and maintain threat models for existing and new products

Security Testing & Validation

  • Perform security testing of web applications, mobile applications, and APIs

  • Conduct static and dynamic application security testing

  • Execute penetration testing and vulnerability assessments

  • Review code for security vulnerabilities and provide remediation guidance

  • Validate security controls and defensive measures

DevSecOps Integration

  • Implement and maintain Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools in CI/CD pipelines

  • Deploy and optimize Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) solutions

  • Establish cloud security best practices and tooling for AWS environments

  • Build security gates and quality checks into development workflows

  • Collaborate with DevOps teams to secure infrastructure as code

Security Automation & Tooling

  • Develop automated security testing frameworks and scripts

  • Build tools and integrations to streamline security processes

  • Automate vulnerability scanning and reporting workflows

  • Create self-service security tools for development teams

  • Implement security orchestration and response automation

Security Analytics & Monitoring

  • Design and implement security metrics and KPIs for product security

  • Analyze security testing results and trends to identify systemic issues

  • Build dashboards and reporting for security posture visibility

  • Conduct security data analysis to inform strategic decisions

  • Monitor and respond to security alerts and incidents

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner with engineering teams to provide security guidance and support

  • Educate developers on secure coding practices and security requirements

  • Work with product managers to balance security and business requirements

  • Collaborate with infrastructure and platform teams on security architecture

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in product security, application security, or related cybersecurity roles

  • Strong background in threat modeling and secure design review.

  • Extensive experience with web application security testing and mobile application security for iOS and Android platforms

  • Hands-on experience with DevSecOps practices and security tool integration

  • Proficiency with SAST, DAST, Cloud Security tools

  • Experience with security automation and scripting (Python, Bash)

  • Background in security analytics and data analysis for security insights

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with container security (Docker, Kubernetes)

  • Knowledge of infrastructure as code security (Terraform, CloudFormation)

  • Familiarity with security frameworks (NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2)

  • Experience with bug bounty programs and responsible disclosure

  • Experience with compliance requirements (PCI DSS, GDPR)

item.title: GRC & Data Privacy Analyst
item.description:
Role Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented GRC & Data Privacy Analyst to join our security team. In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining our integrated risk management framework while taking a lead role in implementing and auditing our data privacy program. You will ensure that our operations remain compliant with global regulations (GDPR, PDPA, etc.) while identifying and mitigating risks across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Governance & Risk Management

  • Framework Alignment: Maintain and mature the organization’s security framework (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2 and Singapore MAS).

  • Risk Assessments: Conduct annual and project-based risk assessments; maintain the Corporate Risk Register and track remediation efforts.

  • Policy Management: Draft, review, and update internal security policies and standards to ensure they reflect current business processes.

  • Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM): Evaluate the security posture of vendors and partners through assessments and due diligence reviews.

Data Privacy Implementation

  • Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs/DPIAs): Lead the evaluation of new products or processes to ensure "Privacy by Design" is integrated into the development lifecycle.

  • Data Mapping: Maintain a comprehensive record of processing activities (ROPA) and data flow diagrams.

  • Privacy Operations: Manage the Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) process and coordinate responses to privacy-related inquiries.

  • Compliance Monitoring: Monitor changes in global privacy laws and translate them into actionable technical or procedural requirements for the IT and Product teams.

Compliance & Auditing

  • Internal Audits: Perform regular control testing to ensure ongoing compliance with internal policies and external regulations.

  • External Audit Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors during certification cycles.

  • Awareness Training: Develop and deliver training content on security best practices and data handling requirements for all employees.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: 8 - 10 years in GRC, Information Security, or IT Audit, with at least 2–4 years specifically focused on Data Privacy.

  • Certifications (Preferred): CISA, CRISC, or CISM.

  • Technical Skills: Familiarity with GRC tools (Sprinto) and a solid understanding of cloud security (AWS).

  • Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of GDPR, PDPA, and industry standards like ISO 27001, SOC 2 and Singapore MAS

Soft Skills for Success

  • The "Translator" Ability: Can explain complex legal requirements to developers and technical risks to executives.

  • Analytical Rigor: A passion for documentation and a "trust but verify" mindset.

  • Adaptability: Comfortable navigating the gray areas of emerging privacy legislation.
